title: Cenote Mul Tun - Roser, Vesely 2016
credits: Cenote Mul Tun, Tulum, Quintana Roo; surveyed April 2, 2016 by Nathan Roser and Carol Vesely; drawn by Juliana Rincón and Peter Sprouse (AMCS Activities Newsletter 39, p. 11, 2016). Length 180 m, depth 6 m.
sistemaWhy: 'Cenote Mul Tun Siphon' (QRSS: 109.7 m, 8.5 m deep, explored 2015-07 by Leal, Reato): this map's cenote has a sump ('sump / sifón') at its south end, which is most likely that siphon. The database also has 'Mul Tun Spring' (-KPZgfx6HrT4lGgouidJ, QRSS: 3084 m, 14.6 m, 2016-01, Leal, Reato), probably the upstream side of the same cenote; the map shows neither passage beyond the sump. Neither sistema has a cave or a position.
wetDry: Mostly underwater: an open collapse (the drip line of T ticks around the white centre, about 35 x 40 m) holds a dry breakdown mound, 'El Mul Tun'; the cave is the ring of overhang around it, flooded (pale blue) except for the stippled breakdown slope at the mound's foot, with a deeper sump (darker blue) at its south end. Water is about half of the whole plan and about three quarters of the roofed part.

walls.why: the cave's outer wall (dashed where low or unsurveyed: 'low / bajo' on the east side, the sump's walls) and the small black columns
pillars and islands standing in the water (dark grey)

notWalls: width 0.18 black: the water's edge along the breakdown slope (not a wall); 0.37 black and dark grey: floor detail (boulders, stipple, stalagmite triangles, speleothem 'flowers', drip-line and ledge ticks), the four cross-sections drawn outside the cave with their leaders, the north arrow's head; 0.51: scale bar; 0.74 black also draws the page frame (excluded); 2.94: an outer border outside the visible page. Blue fills: water (pale) and the sump (darker). The 0.74 black circled cross with 'E' on a boulder at the mound's east foot is a survey station / benchmark symbol, excluded.

entrances.name: Cenote Mul Tun
entrances.why: the open collapse: the drip line (ring of T ticks) around the white centre, with the breakdown mound 'El Mul Tun' in it; the map marks no other opening. No database cave (the database's Multum-Ha near Cobá, -LVKvqj2rgtw2DMCyEnJ, is a different cenote: a closed dome reached by an 18 m staircase, its water up to 17 m deep, vs this open cenote 6 m deep in all)

symbols.why: Vector map: the labels are real PDF text (page.get_text), positions in PDF points. build_layer.py doesn't read symbols yet. No depth numbers on the plan (only 'Depth / Profundidad: 6 m' in the title block), no ceiling heights, no bones (no legend, no bone icon or word), no flow arrows (the only arrow is the diveline tie's leader). The small black triangles are stalagmites.

unverified: No position for this cenote: it isn't in the database (its sistemas 'Cenote Mul Tun Siphon' and 'Mul Tun Spring' have no cave or position), nor in OpenStreetMap, and no placed map shows it; the map only says 'Tulum' (the municipality, which also holds Cobá). The single control point below is a NOMINAL anchor (Tulum town centre, 20.2114 N, 87.4654 W) only so the pipeline can run: the geometry is NOT on the ground. To fix: a field GPS of the cenote (an open collapse about 35 x 40 m with a rock mound in it, which should show as a canopy gap on the satellite once its area is known).
